scope: SLICE-011 claim 1 only (provider watchdog). Disposable prototype; ships nothing.
claimTitle: Provider watchdog: inactivity (idle) + absolute timeout around llm.stream
adr: ADR-015 (proposed 2026-08-06), Decision Outcome (1) and sad-path #1/#11; quality attribute 'Reliability: a provider stalls mid-stream -> run reaches a terminal state within budget'.

artifacts.change: +40/-4; idle guard via Stream.timeoutOrElse (~L236-251), absolute guard via Effect.raceFirst vs failing sleep (~L298-318), ProviderWatchdogConfig off-by-default (~L44-49). RunError union unchanged; both failures typed LLMError.

defect: A stalled provider stream (one chunk then silence) makes llm.stream(request).pipe(Stream.runForEach(...)) block forever, so the run never reaches a terminal state. Baseline proven by the existing manually-interrupted test verifyPartialFlushOnInterruption (session-runner.test.ts:525).

design.idle: Stream.timeoutOrElse({ duration: idle, orElse: () => Stream.fail(LLMError 'Provider stream idle timeout') }) wrapping llm.stream(request). Per-pull deadline that RESETS on every emitted chunk (verified in installed effect@4.0.0-beta.83 dist/Stream.js:2075-2109).
design.absolute: Effect.raceFirst(restore(providerStream), Effect.sleep(absolute).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.fail(LLMError 'Provider turn absolute timeout')))) inside the existing Effect.uninterruptibleMask. On budget elapse the blocked consumer is interrupted (raceAllFirst -> fiberInterruptAll, verified dist/internal/effect.js:948-975).
design.whyNotEffectTimeout: Effect.timeout widens the error type to Cause.TimeoutError, which is outside the RunError/LLMError union and would not satisfy `failure instanceof LLMError`. Both watchdog failures are kept as LLMError so existing failure-handling maps them to a terminal assistant-error state.
design.toggle: ProviderWatchdogConfig (module-level, OFF by default) so existing behavior is byte-identical when idle/absolute are undefined.

fixtures.slowComplete: Stream.fromIterable([stepStart, textStart, textDelta('Complete'), textEnd, stepFinish, finish]).pipe(Stream.tap(() => Effect.sleep('150 millis')))

commands.negative: cd packages/core && bun test test/watchdog-prototype.test.ts -t 'NEGATIVE CONTROL:'
commands.slow: cd packages/core && bun test test/watchdog-prototype.test.ts -t 'SLOW STREAM:'
commands.absoluteActive: cd packages/core && bun test test/watchdog-prototype.test.ts -t 'ABSOLUTE: the absolute timeout cuts an active stream'
commands.absoluteStall: cd packages/core && bun test test/watchdog-prototype.test.ts -t 'ABSOLUTE: with idle off'

RED.meaning: stalled run does not terminate (unsafe baseline)

GREEN.meaning: idle watchdog drives stalled run to terminal state within budget

NEG.meaning: negative control: watchdog off -> still hangs (watchdog is the cause)

SLOW.meaning: healthy slow stream (150ms gaps < idle, 936ms < absolute) is NOT falsely cut

ABS-ACTIVE.meaning: active stream (100ms gaps < idle so idle cannot fire) is cut by the ABSOLUTE budget at ~1000ms, not idle at 400ms

ABS-STALL.meaning: with idle OFF, the absolute budget alone terminates a stall (~800ms) -> absolute is independently effective

regression: session-runner.test.ts: 83 pass / 0 fail (247 expect calls). Watchdog off-by-default leaves verifyPartialFlushOnInterruption and all existing turns byte-identical.
antiDecorationChecks: RED/GREEN/NEG/ABS all drive the real runner.run -> SessionRunner.Service -> runTurnAttempt -> llm.stream(request).pipe(Stream.runForEach(...)); only the LLM transport is faked.
No test asserts a timeout helper's return value; the stall happens inside the real runner stream.
The watchdog toggles the real production path in llm.ts (not a test-only stub).
Fresh DB per test verified: GREEN observes ctxLen=2 in a full-file run (no cross-test contamination).
idleAbsoluteDistinct: GREEN: idle fires on a silent stall at 441ms.
SLOW: idle does NOT false-fire on a 150ms-gap active stream; absolute does NOT fire under 3000ms.
ABS-ACTIVE: on a 100ms-gap active stream idle cannot fire, absolute fires at ~1000ms -> the two mechanisms are observably distinct.
ABS-STALL: with idle disabled, absolute alone terminates -> absolute is independently effective, not a shadow of idle.
provenCodeValidation: Stream.timeoutOrElse is per-pull and resets the deadline on each delivered chunk; keeps error typed LLMError (effect@4.0.0-beta.83 dist/Stream.js:2075-2109) - reviewer-hy3 + reviewer-deepseek.

Effect.raceFirst interrupts the losing fiber via raceAllFirst -> fiberInterruptAll and awaits its death incl. finalizers (dist/internal/effect.js:948-975, :602-608) - reviewer-hy3 + reviewer-deepseek.
forkUnsafe creates race children interruptible regardless of the enclosing mask (dist/internal/effect.js:2075-2088) - reviewer-deepseek.

The installed Stream.timeout doc example itself uses Stream.make(1).pipe(Stream.concat(Stream.never), Stream.timeout('1 second')) (Stream.ts:3536-3545), i.e. the exact stall pattern this watchdog guards.

reviewer-hy3.consensusFinding: Absolute-timeout branch was source-verified correct but never empirically exercised by the original 4-test suite (idle always fired first on silent stalls; SLOW fired neither).
reviewer-hy3.requiredFollowUp: Add a test where only the absolute timeout fires (active-but-over-budget, and absolute-only on a stall with idle off).

reviewer-deepseek.consensusFinding: Same as reviewer-hy3: idle half fully proven; absolute half correct in code but unverified by execution. Also flagged SLOW-test timing headroom (2.67x) and ProviderWatchdogConfig mutable-singleton as residual.

reviewers.consensusResolution: CONSENSUS ACCEPTED (not debated): the finding is specific, correct, and verifiable. CLOSED by adding ABS-ACTIVE (1018ms ~ absolute 1000ms, idle cannot fire on 100ms gaps) and ABS-STALL (827ms ~ absolute 800ms, idle off). Both halves now empirically proven; suite is 6/6 green.

residualRisks: ProviderWatchdogConfig is a module-level mutable singleton, not per-session; acceptable for a disposable prototype, must become real config before any production slice (SLICE-012+).
SLOW test uses real-clock timing with 2.67x headroom (150ms gap vs 400ms idle); low false-cut risk but could flake under extreme scheduler load.
Tool-call-in-flight interaction with a firing watchdog is untested (fixtures are no-tool); out of claim-1 scope, noted for the production slice.
Wall-clock elapsed assertions are timing-sensitive by design (disposable prototype).
This record is claim-1 scoped only. It is NOT the full SLICE-011 EXIT_RECORD: claims 2-5 (reconciler, durable retry, durable blockers, fencing) remain unproven.
notProven: Claims 2-5 of ADR-015 (reconciler reorder, durable retry, durable blockers, Session-ID fencing).
Production integration: a green prototype is not proof of production durability (ADR-015 Scope).
Cross-model failover and subagent/task recovery (deferred by ADR-015).
